title: Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance - CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance - Law of Agency
subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: In the context of public procurement, the purchasing officer typically acts in which of the following capacities on behalf of the government entity?
questions.explain: Under the Law of Agency, the government entity is the 'Principal,' and the public purchaser acts as the 'Agent' who is authorized to make decisions and enter into contracts on the Principal's behalf.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: The fundamental legal duty that an agent owes to their principal—requiring loyalty, care, obedience, and good faith—is known as a(n):
questions.explain: A fiduciary duty is the highest standard of care at either equity or law, requiring the agent to act primarily for the benefit of the principal in matters connected with the agency.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: Which scenario best demonstrates an agent breaching their fiduciary duty to the principal?
options: The agent awards a contract to the lowest responsive and responsible bidder.
The agent unknowingly accepts an offer that contains a minor math error.
The agent routes a public contract to a firm owned by their spouse without disclosing it.
The agent negotiates aggressively to lower the cost of goods for the principal.
questions.explain: Fiduciary duty requires loyalty and putting the principal's interests first. Awarding a contract to a spouse's firm without disclosure creates a massive conflict of interest and breaches the duty of loyalty.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: When an agent terminates the agency relationship by quitting their job at the public procurement office, this termination is classified legally as:
questions.explain: In agency law, 'Renunciation' occurs when the agent terminates the relationship, whereas 'Revocation' occurs when the principal terminates the agent's authority.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: The legal concept that holds a principal liable for the negligent or wrongful acts of an agent acting within the scope of their employment is known as:
questions.explain: 'Respondeat Superior' (let the master answer) is a legal doctrine holding an employer/principal legally responsible for the wrongful acts of an employee/agent if such acts occur within the scope of the employment or agency.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: If a purchasing agent signs a contract knowing it exceeds their legal authority and limits, who could be held personally liable for the obligations in the contract if the public agency refuses to ratify it?
options: No one; the contract simply vanishes.
questions.explain: If an agent acts wholly outside their actual authority and the principal does not ratify the act, the third party (vendor) may sue the agent personally for breach of the implied warranty of authority.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance
